context: Real Image Batch DNA Effect Verification V1: separating DNA-completeness vs. palette/geometry/scorer causes for SHINKAI_01/02 low camera_preservation in services/realImageBatchValidation.ts (the 10-scene real-image-batch-validation pipeline), and adding MORI_04 to its coverage.
finding: camera_preservation in scoreFromPixels() is computed as clampScore(min(horizontal_gradient/2.2, 48) + panEnergy*1200 + cameraEnergy*400 + 32), where panEnergy/cameraEnergy come directly from the UNFLOORED camera_velocity[0]/mean(camera_velocity) read from exports/source_video_dna/camera-behavior-dna/{SOURCE}.json. Checked all 8 batch sources (GHIBLI_01/02/03, SHINKAI_01/02, MORI_01/03, TITANIC_02): every one of their camera-behavior-dna files is the OLD synthetic hash-seeded placeholder schema (dna_id ending "-v2", no source/estimated_only/artifact_type fields) -- there is zero real-vs-synthetic DNA completeness variance to test in this dimension; all 8 are equally synthetic. SHINKAI_01/02 happen to have low seeded camera_velocity[0] values (0.0108/0.01) vs GHIBLI/MORI (~0.026-0.03). Critically, generateProductionPng() FLOORS the same value at 0.032 (effectivePan = max(abs(camVel), 0.032)) before it affects any actual generated pixel content -- so the generated images for ALL 8 sources use the identical 0.032 pan intensity (every source is below the floor). But scoreFromPixels() uses the raw, unfloored value directly as an additive score bonus with no corresponding floor, so SHINKAI scores ~20-25 points lower on the non-gradient term (~45-46 vs ~67-72 for GHIBLI/MORI) for a pixel difference that never actually occurred in the generated image. CONCLUSION: the SHINKAI camera_preservation gap is a scorer-formula floor-asymmetry artifact (generation floors at 0.032, scoring does not), NOT a DNA-completeness effect (no completeness variance exists to test) and NOT a palette/geometry effect (palette RGB and subject_bbox geometry play no role in this formula). The DNA-completeness-improves-generation-fidelity hypothesis is NOT_PROVEN for this metric -- correctly, per instruction, rather than forced. Did NOT touch the scoring formula/floor/thresholds (explicitly out of scope -- would be exactly the forbidden arbitrary score tuning). Separately: added MORI_04 to the batch by SWAPPING it for MORI_03 (not adding an 11th scene) after discovering the pipeline is a rigid, verify-script-enforced fixed-10 benchmark (images=10, ghibli=3/shinkai=2/mori=2/titanic=3 all hardcoded in scripts/verify-real-image-batch-validation.ts) -- appending a scene breaks that invariant and is not actually minimal. MORI_04 scored camera_preservation=100 (its real camera-behavior-dna seed value is in the same high range as MORI_01/03), independently corroborating the diagnosis. Also found MORI_04 already has 5x real coverage in the separate, larger, already-passing 100-scene batch (reports/real_image_batch_100_validation) -- the 10-scene batch was the only one actually missing it.

context: GENIE Retrieval Reliability Repair V1: root-causing and minimally fixing the 4 false-negative + 1 false-positive cases from the fixed 16-event recall benchmark, without fuzzy/RAG/vector search and without trading precision for recall.
finding: Root-caused all 5 failures precisely (measured overlap/contiguous-run for every candidate, not guessed): 3 of 4 false negatives were genuine ties at max token-overlap between multiple real, relevant records, where the old algorithm failed closed to zero instead of returning any of them (e.g. "AIStudio real image generation trial input" tied 5-5 between the AIStudio path-discovery and AIStudio-trial observations). The false positive ("user completed real image app manual review titanic scenes" wrongly matching "Camera Preservation Semantic Alignment V1") was a short, generic 2-3 token coincidence inside an otherwise long, unrelated query. Empirically swept several fix candidates against the fixed benchmark before choosing: raising the contiguous-run threshold to 3 fixed the false positive but reintroduced false negatives (worse than baseline); corpus document-frequency-based stopword filtering had zero effect (the colliding words were not frequent enough corpus-wide to be filtered, given only 11 records exist); multi-match-on-tie alone fixed all 4 false negatives but introduced 1 NEW false positive. The combination that worked and was swept for stability, not picked at a lucky single point: (1) when multiple candidates genuinely tie at max overlap and ALL individually clear the existing contiguous-run>=2 bar, return all of them honestly instead of forcing a single guess or failing to nothing; (2) require overlap to cover at least 60% of the query's own token count (MIN_OVERLAP_RATIO in services/genieUnifiedMemoryRetrieval.mjs) -- stable at 0 false negatives/0 false positives across the ratio range [0.6, 0.65] on the full 16-case benchmark, confirmed by sweeping 0 to 0.75. This uses only the corpus's raw, unfiltered tokens -- no stopword list needed. Deployed and reverified against the real module (not just simulation): 10/10 any-match correct-find, 6/6 true-negative, 0 false positives under the original loose any-match criterion. HOWEVER: went further and checked not just any_match but whether the CORRECT specific record was retrieved for the mandatory AIStudio completion-status case, and found a deeper, separate residual issue -- "AIStudio" (no space, as written throughout this project's actual vocabulary) does not token-match a query phrased "AI Studio" (with space); the query instead uniquely wins on "Next Real Production Task Selection V1" via unrelated generic-word overlap ("did","a","real","image" etc.), never surfacing the "AIStudio First Real Generation Trial V1" record that actually states the correct PENDING status. Tested a general (non-hardcoded) adjacent-token-join normalization as a possible fix -- it did not close this specific gap (both competing records contain the joined form, so the bonus does not break the tie) though it incidentally improved other cases via more honest multi-matching. Did not force a further fix, given the same reliability discipline: promoted the fixed 16-event benchmark (with this stricter per-case content check now included for the mandatory case) to scripts/verify-genie-memory-recall-benchmark-v1.mjs as a permanent regression test. It currently reports 15/16 (1 false negative -- the mandatory AIStudio case, under the stricter check), honestly, not hidden or loosened to force a green result. Per explicit instruction, this is a STOP signal: NOT proceeding to backfill the 95-100 historical episodes from GENIE Historical Memory Bootstrap Assessment V1 until this specific residual gap is separately, deliberately addressed.

context: GENIE Retrieval Identity Normalization V1: focused root-cause analysis of the AIStudio <-> AI Studio recall failure, and testing whether general (non-hardcoded) identifier normalization -- camelCase/PascalCase/acronym-boundary splitting -- can fix it without increasing false positives on the fixed 16-event benchmark.
finding: Root cause confirmed precisely: tokenize() lowercases before extracting alphanumeric runs, so "AIStudio" (as written throughout this project's actual entries, PascalCase, no space) becomes ONE token "aistudio", while a query phrased "AI Studio" (space-separated, as a natural-language user might type it) becomes TWO tokens "ai","studio" -- these never overlap. The query instead wins uniquely on an unrelated record via generic-word coincidence ("did","a","real","image" etc.), never surfacing the "AIStudio First Real Generation Trial V1" record that states the correct PENDING status. Tested three general, non-hardcoded identifier-normalization variants (casing-shape rules, not any specific word), each swept against the real, current 16-event benchmark: (1) full camelCase+acronym boundary splitting (fooBar->foo Bar, AIStudio->AI Studio) applied to replace the original tokenization -- false positives went from 1 to 2 (a NEW record, "GENIE Retrieval Reliability Repair V1" itself, started winning coincidentally on multiple queries because splitting its own filenames/prose created more collision surface corpuswide); (2) acronym-boundary splitting only (AIStudio->AI Studio, no general camelCase rule) -- false positives stayed at 1, but false negatives went from 1 to 2, regressing a previously-passing case ("AIStudio real image generation trial input") because the same GENIE meta-entry now also gained matching tokens and out-competed the correct target; (3) union of original AND split token forms (nothing removed, only added) -- same net result as (1), false positives 1->2. All three fail the explicit "FP 증가 시 STOP/되돌림" bar; none reaches 16/16. No code was shipped -- services/genieUnifiedMemoryRetrieval.mjs is unchanged from commit 51139b6, confirmed via git status before concluding. Deeper finding, more important than the tokenization detail itself: the true blocker is not fundamentally a tokenization-boundary problem. It is that this session's OWN meta/diagnostic Observation entries -- which discuss "AIStudio" and "camera preservation" extensively because they are ABOUT the retrieval-testing and repair work itself -- increasingly dominate matches for those exact topics as more such entries accumulate, competing against and sometimes beating the original substantive entries they are describing. Also confirmed independently of any change made this task: simply re-running the fixed benchmark on the CURRENT corpus (grown by exactly one entry -- this same log's own closing entry from the prior task) already shifted the false-positive case's identity (a different record now wins the same false match) while the count stayed at 1 -- proving the benchmark's pass/fail state is not a one-time-checked-then-stable property; it must be re-verified every time the corpus grows, not just once.
